evidence.claim: Comfort Systems USA's 2025 Form 10-K states that technology-sector demand, particularly data centers, was especially strong; the company reported 2025 backlog of about $11.94 billion and electrical-segment revenue growth.
EMCOR's annual reporting describes data centers within its network and communications market sector and identifies electrical and mechanical construction services as a major project area.
evidence.source_title: EMCOR Group Form 10-K annual report reference

evidence.claim: NuScale's FY2025 reporting states that it completed work on Fluor's Phase 2 FEED study for the RoPower Doicesti project and that Fluor-related agreements remain part of NuScale's disclosures.

BWX Technologies' 2025 Form 10-K describes advanced nuclear reactor technology development, fuel, reactor design, engineering, licensing and manufacturing services for power and propulsion applications.

Cameco's 2025 annual report says it produced 21.0 million pounds of uranium, produced 14.0 million kgU in Fuel Services, added long-term UF6 conversion contracts, and has uranium, fuel services and Westinghouse segments.

Centrus reported completing Phase 2 of its HALEU operation contract with delivery of 900 kilograms of HALEU to DOE and said DOE exercised a Phase 3 portion valued at about $110 million through June 30, 2026.

Nano Nuclear Energy's FY2025 update frames AI data centers and electrification as demand drivers for reliable baseload energy but remains a development-stage microreactor company rather than a deployed commercial generator.
evidence.source_title: NANO Nuclear Reports Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Results and Provides Business Update

evidence.claim: Oklo announced on May 6, 2026 that the NRC approved its Principal Design Criteria topical report for the Aurora powerhouse in Idaho, clearing the report to be referenced in future applications.
evidence.source_title: Oklo’s NRC Principal Design Criteria Topical Report Approved for Aurora Powerhouse in Idaho

evidence.claim: Oklo and Switch announced a strategic relationship for up to 12 GW of advanced nuclear power for AI, cloud and enterprise data-center infrastructure, but this remains subject to deployment execution.
evidence.source_title: Oklo and Switch Form Landmark Strategic Relationship to Deploy 12 Gigawatts of Advanced Nuclear Power

evidence.claim: Amazon's 2025 Form 10-K reported cash capital expenditures of $128.3 billion in 2025, primarily reflecting technology infrastructure investments, most of which support AWS growth.
Talen announced an expanded nuclear power purchase agreement to provide carbon-free electricity from Susquehanna to AWS data centers supporting AI and cloud technologies.
evidence.source_title: Talen Energy 8-K: Expanded Nuclear Energy Relationship with Amazon

evidence.claim: Microsoft stated in January 2025 that it was on track to invest approximately $80 billion in FY2025 to build AI-enabled datacenters for training AI models and deploying AI and cloud applications.
evidence.source_title: The golden opportunity for American AI

evidence.claim: Constellation announced a 20-year PPA with Microsoft to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 as the Crane Clean Energy Center, with Microsoft purchasing energy to match data-center power use in PJM.
evidence.source_title: Constellation to Launch Crane Clean Energy Center

evidence.claim: Google announced a corporate agreement with Kairos Power to purchase nuclear energy from multiple SMRs, targeting up to 500 MW of 24/7 carbon-free power for U.S. grids to support data centers and offices.
evidence.source_title: Google signs advanced nuclear clean energy agreement with Kairos Power

evidence.claim: Google announced a data-center and clean-energy growth approach with Intersect Power and TPG Rise Climate to develop industrial parks with gigawatts of U.S. data-center capacity co-located with new clean-energy plants.
evidence.source_title: Google announces new approach to data center and clean energy growth

evidence.claim: Meta's 2025 Form 10-K disclosed $131.05 billion of contractual commitments as of December 31, 2025, mostly related to cloud capacity arrangements and investments in servers, network infrastructure, data centers and Reality Labs hardware.

Meta announced nuclear energy agreements with Vistra, TerraPower and Oklo following its nuclear RFP process, describing up to 6.6 GW of new and existing clean energy by 2035 to support AI and data-center operations.
evidence.source_title: Meta Announces Nuclear Energy Projects, Unlocking Up to 6.6 GW to Power American Leadership in AI Innovation

memory_update.text: FIX and EME are the strongest mechanical/electrical construction mappings in this chunk; both should be tracked through backlog/RPO mix, labor capacity, data-center customer concentration and margin conversion rather than treated as generic AI plays.
AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL and META are best used as demand-side validation and procurement-signal tickers for AI data centers, power, grid and nuclear, not as pure bottleneck suppliers.

BWXT, CCJ and LEU form the more credible nuclear supply-chain subgroup: BWXT for components/services/fuel, CCJ for uranium/conversion/Westinghouse, and LEU for HALEU/enrichment; all require separation of AI-driven demand from broader nuclear-cycle demand.

FLR needs direct project-level verification before ranking higher: confirm funded nuclear/power EPC awards, Fluor's economic exposure to NuScale, and any connection between power projects and hyperscaler or data-center load.
OKLO and NNE remain early-stage/speculative until licensing, fuel, financing, binding offtake, engineering validation and first deployment milestones are independently confirmed.

For this chunk, next Layer 2C checks should include market-pricing/crowding: relative performance, valuation expansion, earnings revision dependence, short interest and whether AI power narratives are already embedded.

summary: Layer 2B maps this candidate chunk into three relationship clusters: (1) mechanical/electrical execution capacity for AI data-center construction, where FIX and EME have the most direct public-market relationship; (2) nuclear/firm-power supply-chain exposure, where BWXT, CCJ and LEU are upstream or enabling nodes and FLR is an EPC/engineering node with less direct AI-data-center linkage; and (3) hyperscaler demand and power-procurement signal issuers, where AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL and META validate the grid, firm-power, construction and nuclear procurement themes but are not themselves pure bottleneck suppliers. OKLO and NNE remain speculative/early-stage mappings that require licensing, fuel, customer, financing and deployment evidence before being treated as validated chokepoints.
